articles.title: 🧠 A.I. Lab Unveils Its Best Model Yet And Declares 'The Age Of AGI Has Begun'; The Press Release Is Extremely Confident, The Definition Slightly Less So
articles.dateline: SAN FRANCISCO — reported from the dawn of something, allegedly
paras: A leading A.I. lab launched what it calls its most capable model ever and, in the same breath, announced that humanity has officially entered "the age of artificial general intelligence" — a milestone so momentous that nobody in the room could fully agree on what it means, only that we are definitely in it now.

"This changes everything," the company said, of a threshold it has been announcing the imminent arrival of for several years running. Experts note the peculiar genius of the moment: we have built a machine smart enough to be called generally intelligent, yet the humans remain locked in a decade-long debate over what that phrase actually is — which may, in the end, be the most convincing proof that people are still in charge.

articles.title: 🪥 Famous Vacuum Company Unveils Its First Toothbrush; The Relentless War On Household Dust Has Officially Reached Your Molars
articles.dateline: THE BATHROOM SINK — reported at high RPM
paras: A company legendary for reinventing the vacuum cleaner, the hair dryer, and the hand dryer has now turned its formidable engineering might toward the humble toothbrush — because apparently there was one remaining corner of your home not yet occupied by a sleek, expensive, powerfully whirring device.

"We saw an opportunity to do it properly," the company said, of a market that many people assumed had been comfortably solved for about a century. Analysts note the firm's unstoppable logic: identify a common object, add a tiny motor and a premium price, and reveal that you had been living wrong the entire time. The teeth, for their part, could not be reached for comment, but were reportedly very clean.

articles.title: 💸 Chipmaker's Pile Of Investments Swells To $99 Billion; The Company Is Now Quietly A Shareholder In Roughly The Entire Future
articles.dateline: THE CAP TABLE — reported from every startup at once
paras: The world's most valuable chipmaker has grown its portfolio of investments to a staggering sum, pouring money into so many A.I. companies that it is now, in a very real sense, a part-owner of nearly everyone building the technology that runs on its chips.

"We're investing in the ecosystem," the company said, of a strategy in which it sells the shovels, funds the miners, and owns a slice of the mine. Analysts note the arrangement has achieved a kind of financial perpetual motion: money flows out to startups, who spend it on chips, which flows back as revenue, which flows out again as investment — a beautiful closed loop that everyone agrees is completely fine and definitely not a circle.

articles.title: 📱 New Flagship Phone Arrives With Even More A.I. Inside; The Camera Now Forms Opinions About Your Lunch Before You Do
articles.dateline: THE UNBOXING TABLE — reported to a camera that was already judging it
paras: A major phone maker unveiled its newest flagship, packed with still more on-device A.I. — a device so intelligent that it not only takes a photo of your meal but quietly assesses its composition, lighting, and, one suspects, your life choices.

"It anticipates what you need," the company said, of a phone that increasingly acts less like a tool and more like a well-meaning acquaintance who has thoughts. Experts note the modern flagship has crossed a subtle line: it used to wait for you to press the button, and now it stands ready to help, suggest, enhance, and gently improve every moment before you've even decided the moment was happening.

articles.title: 🦿 Tech Expo Shows Off Wearable Robot Legs; The Exoskeleton Has Arrived, Primarily To Help You Stand Around Looking At The Exoskeleton
articles.dateline: BERLIN — reported from a very sturdy trade-show floor
paras: Europe's giant tech expo dazzled crowds with a parade of futuristic gadgets, none more eye-catching than the wearable exoskeletons — strap-on robotic legs promising to make walking, lifting, and standing dramatically easier, assuming you can first figure out how to put them on.

"It augments the human body," exhibitors said, of a device that turns a stroll to the fridge into a demonstration of the future. Analysts note the exoskeleton captures the whole spirit of the show: a hall full of extraordinary machines engineered to solve problems you didn't know you had, worn by people who mostly just wanted to see if it looked as cool as it did in the brochure. It did.

horoscopes.text: The age of AGI begins today, or so you were told. Nothing on your calendar has changed. Proceed as generally intelligent as ever.
A device you did not know you needed will be revealed as essential. Resist. Your toothbrush was fine. It was always fine.
Someone will invest $99 billion today. It will not be you. But your morning coffee is, technically, part of the ecosystem now.

tech_tip: Before you believe 'the age of AGI has begun,' ask what it means. Nobody will agree. That's the tip. Before you buy robot legs, make sure the fridge is worth it.
gadget_watch: This week's gadget flood: a vacuum company's first toothbrush, a phone that judges your lunch, and wearable robot legs. Your bathroom, your kitchen, and your walking are all now premium subscriptions waiting to happen.
